quotes: The RPM Friction Pro V2 is an updated version that offers more power and pop than the original Friction Pro while maintaining the Gen 3 feel that many high-level players prefer.
It's clearly better than the original Friction Pro in terms of power and pop, and it has a feel profile that I think a lot of players will really like.
pros: More power and pop than original Friction Pro
Elite spin from Gen 3 rough carbon face
Great feel on flicks and speedups
Solid and stable out of the box
cons: Slightly trickier to dial in on dinks than V1
Not as plush feeling on resets as original
written_reviews.disclosure: Play-tested by pro James Ignatowich. 5-10% improvement from original Friction Pro.

written_reviews.author: John Kew
quotes: RPM's Friction Pro Elongated V2 is heavier, more head-heavy, and built on a revised carbon fiber layup.
Friction Pro Elongated V2 16mm: Swing weight 122.2 · Twist weight 6.6 · Spin 2,279 RPM · Surface roughness 8.33 Ra
pros: Highest surface roughness (8.33 Ra) in tests
Heavier swing weight (122.2) for more plow
Improved from V1: more power, better layup
cons: Heavier and more head-heavy than V1
Less comfortable on dinks than original

paddles.name: Pakle Fuse Hybrid W
paddles.description: New brand delivering elite foam-core performance at budget price. DuraSpin Tier 1 grit, 107 swing weight, soft and hollow feel.

written_reviews.author: Braydon Unsicker
quotes: Tier 1 grit durability at $119, a result more commonly found on far more expensive paddles.
One of the quickest power paddles I've measured. Its 107 swing weight belongs on a control paddle; its pace does not.
Soft, hollow impact with a deep thonk, an uncommon feel for a paddle with this much power.
The Fuse Hybrid W is for players who want power without slowing down at the kitchen.
pros: Tier 1 DuraSpin grit at $119 — exceptional value
Quick 107 swing weight — unusual for power
cons: New brand — limited long-term durability data
written_reviews.disclosure: All measurements taken in-house using standardized equipment. Independent testing, no brand payment.

consensus_topics.consensus: Tier 1 DuraSpin — 95% retention, matches paddles twice the price
107 swing weight is in widebody territory for a power paddle
Tier 1 grit at $119 is exceptional — among the best value propositions

paddles.name: Honolulu J2NF Hybrid
paddles.description: All-court foam paddle with soft/dense feel, oversized sweet spot, and activated power. Gold Award winner on All-Court Hot List.

written_reviews.author: Braydon Unsicker
quotes: The forgiveness to swing weight combination is the whole story: a 6.67 twist weight at a 110 swing weight (19th percentile).
A soft, dense, medium plush feel that isn't muted to the point of losing feedback.
Activated power rather than raw pop, so you can swing freely and still keep the ball in the court.
The NF is Honolulu's easiest recommendation — a Gold Award winner on my all-court Hot List.
pros: Soft/dense medium plush feel — comfortable and controlled
Gold Award winner, easy to trust
cons: Raw carbon peel ply — Tier 4 grit durability (wears faster)
Lower swing weight means less plow-through than heavier paddles
written_reviews.disclosure: All measurements taken in-house using standardized equipment. Independent testing, no brand payment.

consensus_topics.consensus: Best forgiveness-to-swing-weight pairing — 6.67 twist at 110 swing weight
Soft/dense medium plush — comfortable without being muted
Raw carbon peel ply is Tier 4 — spin fades faster than durable grit

paddles.name: Six Zero Coral Pro Hybrid
paddles.description: All-Court+ with Diamond Tough Grit Tier 1 durability. Best blend in the Coral Pro series — forgiving, spin-heavy, easy to trust.

written_reviews.author: Braydon Unsicker
quotes: The best blend in the series: a 6.79 twist weight (78th percentile) gives it a notably forgiving sweet spot for a hybrid.
Very high spin (2,062 RPM) on Diamond Tough Grit, which held 95% of its Ra grit in my testing versus the 81% raw-carbon average.
Added offense and spin over the original Coral that don't come at the expense of control.
The Hybrid is the standout of the lineup and the shape I'd hand most players.
pros: Soft/dense feel — easy to trust at the net
cons: Diamond Tough Grit slightly heavier feel
written_reviews.disclosure: All measurements taken in-house using standardized equipment. Independent testing, no brand payment.

consensus_topics.consensus: 6.79 twist weight — 78th percentile, best in Coral Pro series
Diamond Tough Grit Tier 1 — 95% retention, among best tested
Best all-around shape — forgiving, spin-heavy, controllable

paddles.name: Ronbus Tenon R3.16
paddles.description: Gen 4 foam with mortise-and-tenon construction. NanoBond Tier 3 grit, soft/dense feel at power level, 94th percentile firepower.

written_reviews.author: Braydon Unsicker
quotes: The most power in the series at 57.1 MPH, 94th percentile, and the shape that gets the most out of the elongated leverage.
A soft, dense feel is rare at this power level, where almost everything else is stiff and hollow.
Durable grit at a price where you usually don't get it, holding 88% of its Ra grit level.
The R3.16 if you want the most drive velocity in the Tenon line with elongated leverage, durable grit, and USAP approval well under what other durable grit paddles cost.
pros: Soft/dense feel — rare at this power level
cons: Heaviest swinging shape in Tenon line (119 swing weight)
High power can be hard to control for some players
Mid-level pop — not ideal for compact shots
written_reviews.disclosure: All measurements taken in-house using standardized equipment. Independent testing, no brand payment.

consensus_topics.consensus: 94th percentile firepower — most powerful in Tenon line
Soft/dense at power level — unique among power paddles
NanoBond Tier 3 — 88% retention, good for price

paddles.name: Selkirk LUXX Control Air Invikta
paddles.description: Control-oriented elongated paddle with InfiniGrit carbon fiber surface. Best for players who prioritize precision, resets, and dinks over raw power.

Paddle Shape Differences | LUXX Control Air | S2 vs Epic Vs Invikta
Selkirk Luxx Control Air Review! Before You Buy Pros and Cons

written_reviews.author: Chris Olson
quotes: I immediately noticed how much more solid it felt than the 003. It didn't have that tingy hollow feeling nearly as much.
After using so many power paddles this year I had forgotten how much easier something like this is to control. I felt like a reset machine on the court.
I could get the ball to go where I wanted without having to be as conscious about my grip pressure.
The most frustrating area for me was counters at the kitchen line. Since it doesn't have a ton of pop, I just felt like my opponent would consistently get the better of me.
pros: Solid, robust feel (no hollow tingy feeling)
Good spin (1895 RPM with InfiniGrit surface)
cons: Lower power compared to thermoformed/foam-core paddles
Edge sweet spot is more jarring than thermoformed paddles
Edgeless design limits sweet spot size
Paint grit wears down over time
Struggles in hand battles at the kitchen line

consensus_topics.consensus: The LUXX Control Air excels at precision play — resets and drops feel effortless, making it ideal for players who prioritize placement over power.
Compared to foam-core and thermoformed paddles, the Control Air generates noticeably less power, especially in counters and drives.
The edgeless design results in a smaller sweet spot. Edge hits are jarring compared to thermoformed paddles, though lead tape can improve stability.

paddles.name: Selkirk OMNI Elongated
paddles.core_material: ReactCore™ (PureFoam floating center + PureFoam Ring + EVA Power Ring)
paddles.description: Premium all-court foam paddle with adjustable MOI weights and ReactCore double-ring technology. Offers a controlled, feel-first response that tones down the Boomstik's raw power while maintaining strong spin and stability.

written_reviews.author: Team Kitchen
quotes: The Omni prioritizes feel and controllability over raw power and features removable/repositionable weights that let you customize swing weight, stability and power in seconds without tungsten tape or tools.
Players who want a controllable, feel-first paddle they can customize without tungsten tape or tools.
cons: Removable weights may loosen over time
written_reviews.disclosure: Play-tested by multiple 5.0+ players across all shot types.

written_reviews.author: John Kew
quotes: The OMNI successfully tones down the Boomstik's power while maintaining much of the same feel and identity.
It reads 2,364 RPM to the Boomstik's 2,306, both comfortably in Elite territory.
pros: Higher twist weight (7.06) than Boomstik for more stability
Adjustable MOI system lets you customize feel
cons: Potential edge guard durability concerns observed in testing
written_reviews.disclosure: Independently measured using calibrated lab equipment. 400+ paddles tested since 2021. No sponsor influence.
